newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab says props unable to beat jets.
newsitem.headline: Saab says props unable to beat jets.

text.p: Swedish regional turbo-prop plane maker Saab said it has been unable to beat jets in the 50 to 100 passenger market, particularly in North America.
Saab, owned by investment company Investor, said the market for regional aircraft was growing and Saab was receiving positive feedback for its Saab 2000 plane from passengers.

"However we have so far been unable to utilise this experience advantageously against the competition from jets, which today dominate the market for 50-100 passengers, particularly in North America," Saab President Bengt Halse said in a statement.
Halse said conditions were made tougher by excess production capacity and large fleets of secondhand aircraft.
"Nevertheless the Saab 340 has maintained its position during 1996 as a leader in the 30-passenger segment," he added.
